project.name: squadron-ai
project.description: Squadron is a template-driven code review framework that runs repeatable, structured LLM reviews from the terminal through the `sq` CLI. Each review executes a YAML-defined template against a diff, design document, or task plan and returns a verdict (PASS, CONCERNS, or FAIL) with severity-tagged findings. Beyond reviews it orchestrates multi-step agent pipelines across multiple LLM providers, with event streaming, metrology, and an MCP/FastAPI server surface.

nodes.name: load_template

nodes.name: _validate_status_if_present
nodes.summary: Rejects a frontmatter update whose status value is not one of the canonical DocumentStatus members, resolving known aliases first.

nodes.name: split_document

nodes.name: read_frontmatter
nodes.summary: Reads a file and returns its parsed frontmatter mapping, raising FrontmatterError when the block is absent or malformed.

nodes.name: yaml_safe
nodes.summary: Quotes or escapes a scalar so it round-trips safely as a YAML frontmatter value.

nodes.name: render_frontmatter_block
nodes.summary: Renders a mapping back into a fenced YAML frontmatter block with stable key ordering.

nodes.name: update_frontmatter
nodes.summary: Rewrites selected frontmatter fields of a document in place, validating status values and stamping the current date.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Single canonical definition of the document status and docType frontmatter values squadron emits, referenced by every review, devlog, and evidence writer.

nodes.name: DocumentStatus
nodes.summary: StrEnum of the five canonical lifecycle status values a process document's frontmatter may hold.

nodes.name: DocType
nodes.summary: StrEnum of the canonical docType values squadron writes into generated documents.

nodes.name: logging.py
nodes.summary: Structured logging configuration for the framework, providing a single-line JSON formatter and the shared logger factory used across every module.

nodes.name: _JsonFormatter
nodes.summary: Logging formatter that renders each record as a single-line JSON object with UTC timestamp and level.

nodes.name: setup_logging
nodes.summary: Configures root logging handlers and level from settings, selecting JSON or plain formatting.

nodes.name: devlog.py

nodes.name: DevlogAction
nodes.summary: Pipeline action implementing the devlog step: validates its config and appends a structured entry to DEVLOG.md.

nodes.name: _auto_generate
nodes.summary: Builds a devlog entry body automatically from the pipeline action context when no explicit entry was supplied.

nodes.name: _read_or_create
nodes.summary: Reads DEVLOG.md, creating it with correct frontmatter and heading when it does not yet exist.

nodes.name: _insert_entry

nodes.name: _find_content_start
nodes.summary: Locates the line index where devlog content begins, skipping frontmatter and the document title.

nodes.name: GateEvidence

nodes.name: gate_evidence_frontmatter
nodes.summary: Builds the YAML frontmatter mapping for a gate-evidence artifact from a GateEvidence record.

nodes.name: render_gate_evidence
nodes.summary: Renders a GateEvidence record as the full markdown artifact including its frontmatter block.

nodes.name: save_gate_evidence
nodes.summary: Writes the rendered gate-evidence artifact to the reviews directory under a name kept outside the *-review.* glob.

nodes.summary: Resolves the gate step's judge model through the ActionContext resolver cascade, surfacing resolution failures explicitly.

nodes.name: judge_residue
nodes.summary: Resolves the model and profile for the gate step, then delegates to the shared judge transport for the unsettled residue.

nodes.name: policy.py
nodes.summary: The findings-addressed gate policy: sequences zero-cost deterministic screens before the paid judge leg and derives the verdict from per-finding statuses rather than the model's declaration.

nodes.name: FindingsAddressedPolicy
nodes.summary: Gate policy that runs the deterministic screens, judges only the residue, verifies the claims, and derives the gate verdict from finding statuses.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers the findings-addressed policy with the gate policy registry at import time.

nodes.name: screens.py
nodes.summary: Loop-specific deterministic screens for the gate policy — the no-prior-round screen and the reviewer-re-found-it screen — which settle findings before any model call.

nodes.name: screen_no_prior_round
nodes.summary: Screen 0: settles the first iteration of a loop, where there is no prior round whose findings could have been addressed.

nodes.name: run_deterministic_screens
nodes.summary: Runs the loop-context screens in order over the prior findings, returning the settled outcomes and the residue left for the judge.

nodes.name: _match_key
nodes.summary: Derives the normalized comparison key used to decide whether a fresh finding is the same finding as a prior one.

nodes.name: screen_exact_match
nodes.summary: Screen 2: settles any prior finding the fresh review re-found verbatim, which proves the work did not address it.

nodes.name: review.py
nodes.summary: Pipeline action that runs a structured review inside a pipeline step: resolves the model, slice inputs, and rules, executes the template, then persists the review file and enforces judge thresholds.

nodes.name: ReviewAction
nodes.summary: Pipeline action that resolves model, slice inputs and rules, executes a review template, persists the result, and enforces judge thresholds.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel exposing the shared findings-addressed vocabulary — statuses, finding records, judge parsing, claim verification, and transport — consumed by both the gate loop and the interactive resolve path.

nodes.name: judge.py
nodes.summary: Context-free transport that consults a judge on the residue the deterministic screens could not settle, routing through run_review_with_profile and deliberately never persisting the output as a review file.

nodes.name: JudgeLegResult
nodes.summary: Result of one judge leg: the per-finding outcomes, whether parsing failed, and the raw output kept for evidence.

nodes.name: _render_findings
nodes.summary: Renders the residue finding records into the compact list the judge prompt expects.

nodes.name: judge_residue_core
nodes.summary: Context-free judge transport: builds the prompt, calls run_review_with_profile, parses the status lines, and returns the leg result without persisting anything.

nodes.name: keys.py
nodes.summary: Central registry of every persistent Squadron configuration key, each declared with its type, default value, and human-readable description.

nodes.name: ConfigKey
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one configuration key: its name, expected Python type, default value, and description.

nodes.name: get_default
nodes.summary: Returns the declared default value for a configuration key, raising on unknown keys rather than falling back silently.

nodes.name: manager.py
nodes.summary: Layered configuration manager that merges user-level and project-level TOML files with declared defaults, and reads, writes, and unsets typed config values.
nodes.languageNotes: Precedence is project TOML over user TOML over declared default, with resolve_config_source exposing which layer won.

nodes.name: _config_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the user-level configuration directory, honouring XDG-style overrides before falling back to the platform home directory.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Loads and merges user and project TOML configuration into a single mapping of key to value.

nodes.name: get_config
nodes.summary: Returns the effective value for a configuration key after layer merging and default resolution.

nodes.name: get_typed_config
nodes.summary: Returns a configuration value coerced to the requested type, validating that the declared key type matches.

nodes.name: set_config
nodes.summary: Writes a configuration key to either the project or user TOML file, creating the file and parent directories as needed.

nodes.name: unset_config
nodes.summary: Removes a configuration key from the project or user TOML file, leaving the other layer untouched.

nodes.name: resolve_config_source
nodes.summary: Reports which layer — project, user, or declared default — supplies the effective value for a key.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the metrology data layer, re-exporting the capture, identity, store, model, and error surface so CLI and MCP callers share one import site.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberate surface-agnostic facade so the CLI and MCP surfaces reach identical behaviour by construction.

nodes.name: audit.py
nodes.summary: Drives an end-to-end audit oracle run: resolves the audit skill and profile, preflights the target repository, dispatches the audit agent, and records the resulting findings run.
nodes.languageNotes: The audit prompt is hashed so every recorded run is attributable to the exact prompt text that produced it.

nodes.name: resolve_audit_skill
nodes.summary: Locates the audit skill definition on disk, raising AuditSkillError when it cannot be found.

nodes.name: audit_prompt_hash
nodes.summary: Computes a stable content hash of the audit skill prompt so recorded runs stay attributable to their exact prompt.

nodes.name: find_audit_file
nodes.summary: Searches the target project for the audit artifact file produced by the agent, optionally restricted to files newer than a timestamp.

nodes.name: _is_audit_artifact
nodes.summary: Classifies a git status line as an audit artifact so generated output does not count as a dirty working tree.

nodes.name: preflight_project
nodes.summary: Validates the target repository before an audit runs: derives project identity, checks the working tree is clean, and confirms the expected commit SHA.

nodes.name: extract_audit_protocol
nodes.summary: Extracts the audit protocol section from the skill document body for embedding in the dispatch prompt.

nodes.name: build_audit_prompt
nodes.summary: Assembles the full audit dispatch prompt from the skill protocol and run-independence instructions.

nodes.name: resolve_audit_profile
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective audit provider profile from an explicit argument or persistent configuration.

nodes.name: resolve_audit_model
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective model id for an audit run from an explicit argument or persistent configuration.

nodes.name: _collect_audit_output
nodes.summary: Streams the audit agent's output, forwarding tool events and byte counts to the progress callback while accumulating the response text.

nodes.name: run_audit
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a complete audit run end to end — preflight, prompt build, agent dispatch, finding parse, and persistence — returning a structured success or failure result.

nodes.name: AuditRunResult
nodes.summary: Result envelope for an audit run carrying the recorded run, any failure detail, and rate-limit summary, with a succeeded predicate.

nodes.name: AuditRunFailure
nodes.summary: Enumerates the distinct ways an audit run can fail so callers branch on a typed cause rather than message text.

nodes.name: audit_delta.py
nodes.summary: Computes the per-category delta between a stored audit baseline and a new audit run, marking changes that fall within the measured noise floor.
nodes.languageNotes: Deltas inside the noise floor are flagged rather than hidden, so an operator sees the measurement uncertainty explicitly.

nodes.name: is_within_floor
nodes.summary: Determines whether an observed count delta is small enough to be indistinguishable from measurement noise.

nodes.name: compute_delta
nodes.summary: Builds a full delta report comparing a baseline to a new run, producing per-category cells and totals annotated with noise-floor status.

nodes.name: audit_models.py
nodes.summary: Typed Pydantic output surface for the audit oracle — baselines, delta reports, and pre-emption fragments — kept in one import site so JSON output serialises verbatim.
nodes.languageNotes: Audit severity is deliberately kept disjoint from review severity; the two vocabularies grade different artifacts and are never mapped onto each other.

nodes.name: ProjectBaseline
nodes.summary: A project's audit baseline: the recorded finding counts per category at a given commit, with the noise floor measured for that grouping.

nodes.name: BaselineReport
nodes.summary: Aggregated baseline report across projects, paired with a summary of what was excluded and why.

nodes.name: DeltaReport
nodes.summary: Comparison of a baseline against a newer audit run: per-category deltas, totals, noise-floor status, and an interpretation disclaimer.

nodes.name: PreemptionFragment
nodes.summary: A frozen block of static pre-emption guidance stamped with the baseline identity and timestamp it was generated from.

nodes.name: FreshnessResult
nodes.summary: Outcome of comparing a stored pre-emption fragment against the current baseline, reporting whether the fragment is still current.

nodes.name: audit_parse.py
nodes.summary: Parses the audit agent's free-form YAML findings block into typed AuditFinding records, normalising category, severity, effort, and location vocabularies.
nodes.languageNotes: Lenient parsing by design: prose scalars are quoted before YAML load so unescaped agent text does not break the whole block.

nodes.name: normalize_category
nodes.summary: Maps a raw agent-supplied category string onto the canonical AuditCategory enum, tracking values that fail to normalise.

nodes.name: normalize_severity
nodes.summary: Maps a raw severity string onto the audit's own critical/high/medium/low scale.

nodes.name: normalize_effort
nodes.summary: Maps a raw effort estimate string onto the canonical AuditEffort enum.

nodes.name: normalize_location
nodes.summary: Normalises a finding's location string into a consistent path-and-line form.

nodes.name: _extract_block_body
nodes.summary: Pulls the fenced findings block out of the raw agent response text.

nodes.name: _quote_prose_scalars
nodes.summary: Pre-quotes free-prose YAML scalar values so unescaped agent text parses instead of raising.

nodes.name: _coerce_str
nodes.summary: Coerces a loosely typed YAML value into a trimmed string, rejecting structures that cannot be a scalar.

nodes.name: parse_audit_findings
nodes.summary: Parses the full audit findings block into typed findings, normalising every field and counting values that could not be normalised.

nodes.name: audit_report.py
nodes.summary: Builds the audit baseline report by grouping stored audit runs with their matching noise floors and applying project and category filters.

nodes.name: baseline_report
nodes.summary: Groups stored audit runs by project, commit, and prompt hash, joins each group to its noise floor, and emits a filtered baseline report with exclusion counts.

nodes.name: audit_variance.py
nodes.summary: Reduces repeated audit runs over identical inputs into a measured noise floor, capturing the run-to-run variance in finding counts per category.
nodes.languageNotes: Requires uniform project, commit, and prompt hash across the input runs so variance measures the oracle, not the target.

nodes.name: _require_uniform
nodes.summary: Asserts that every run in the set shares the same value for an identity field, raising AuditVarianceError otherwise.

nodes.name: _stat
nodes.summary: Computes min, max, mean, and standard deviation over a list of counts.

nodes.name: reduce_noise_floor
nodes.summary: Reduces a set of repeated audit runs into an AuditNoiseFloor with total and per-category variance statistics.

nodes.name: calibration.py
nodes.summary: Turns measured agreement evidence into advisory judge threshold recommendations, reading current template thresholds and classifying whether to graduate, tighten, or hold.
nodes.languageNotes: Recommendations are directional and advisory only — never a computed numeric floor the operator is forced to accept.

nodes.name: classify_direction
nodes.summary: Classifies a group's measured match rate into a graduate, tighten, or hold recommendation, respecting the minimum-evidence floor.

nodes.name: read_current_thresholds
nodes.summary: Reads the judge threshold values currently declared in a review template.

nodes.name: read_current_template_content_hash
nodes.summary: Computes the content hash of a review template so recommendations stay pinned to the exact template version measured.

nodes.name: _model_dimension_note
nodes.summary: Builds an explanatory note when a template's measured evidence spans more than one model.

nodes.name: recommend_thresholds
nodes.summary: Produces the full threshold recommendation report from an agreement report, one cell per comparable group with rationale and evidence.

nodes.name: calibration_models.py
nodes.summary: Typed Pydantic shapes for calibration output — recommendation directions, threshold targets, and residual offer targets — so JSON output is emitted verbatim.

nodes.name: RecommendationDirection
nodes.summary: Enumerates the advisory directions a threshold recommendation can take.

nodes.name: ThresholdRecommendation
nodes.summary: One group's advisory recommendation: the direction, the supporting evidence, the target template, and the rationale.

nodes.name: RecommendationReport
nodes.summary: Full calibration report of recommendation cells, exclusions, and whether the evidence floor was applied.

nodes.name: capture.py
nodes.summary: Captures human ground-truth verdicts against judge review artifacts: resolves the target review, builds the capture payload, and records a sample into the metrology store.
nodes.languageNotes: Supports blind capture, where the judge's own verdict is withheld until reveal, so the human verdict is not anchored by it.

nodes.name: resolve_target
nodes.summary: Resolves a user-supplied target into a specific review artifact file, disambiguating by review type when multiple candidates match.

nodes.name: _candidates_by_type
nodes.summary: Groups candidate review files by their declared review type.

nodes.name: _read_review_type
nodes.summary: Reads a candidate review file's declared review type from its frontmatter.

nodes.name: build_capture_payload
nodes.summary: Builds the capture payload for a review file, deriving its result reference and the ground-truth text shown to the human.

nodes.name: record_sample
nodes.summary: Records a human verdict as a SampleVerdict in the metrology store, honouring blind capture and reporting when the sample budget is reached.

nodes.name: reveal
nodes.summary: Reveals the judge's own verdict for a review file after a blind capture has been recorded.

nodes.name: discovery.py
nodes.summary: Discovers judge result artifacts on disk under the project's review directory so they can be offered for ground-truth capture.

nodes.name: discover_judge_results
nodes.summary: Walks the project's review output directory and returns every discovered judge result artifact path.

nodes.name: errors.py
nodes.summary: Typed exception hierarchy for the metrology layer covering identity, target resolution, store, and audit block parsing failures.
nodes.languageNotes: A single MetrologyError root lets callers catch the whole layer while still branching on specific causes.

nodes.name: graduation.py
nodes.summary: Manages judge configuration graduation: writes and looks up graduated configs in the store, and selects residual review offers for continued sampling after graduation.
nodes.languageNotes: Residual sampling continues at a reduced rate after graduation so drift is still detectable.

nodes.name: _identity_matches
nodes.summary: Compares a stored graduated config against a wanted judge config and artifact level for identity equality.

nodes.name: write_graduation
nodes.summary: Persists a graduated judge configuration record into the metrology store.

nodes.name: _review_reviewtype
nodes.summary: Reads a review artifact's declared review type for residual offer filtering.

nodes.name: select_residual_offers
nodes.summary: Selects which discovered judge results to offer for residual sampling, deterministically applying the configured residual rate.

nodes.name: identity.py
nodes.summary: Derives the stable identities metrology records are keyed by — project id from the git remote, judge result references, and judge config ids from template and model.
nodes.languageNotes: Identity is derived from a canonical projection of frontmatter, so cosmetic edits to a review artifact do not change its recorded identity.

nodes.name: _read_git_remote_url
nodes.summary: Reads the origin remote URL from the git repository at the given working directory.

nodes.name: normalize_remote_url
nodes.summary: Normalises SSH and HTTPS git remote URLs into one canonical host-and-path form.

nodes.name: derive_project_id
nodes.summary: Derives the stable project identifier from the git remote, falling back to an explicitly marked local-path source.

nodes.name: read_review_frontmatter
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the YAML frontmatter of a review artifact, raising a typed identity error when it is absent or malformed.

nodes.name: _canonical_projection
nodes.summary: Projects review frontmatter onto the canonical subset of fields that define its identity, so cosmetic edits do not change the hash.

nodes.name: _relative_review_path
nodes.summary: Converts an absolute review artifact path into the project-relative form stored in records.

nodes.name: derive_result_ref
nodes.summary: Builds a JudgeResultRef binding a review artifact to its project, relative path, and content hash.

nodes.name: template_content_hash
nodes.summary: Computes the content hash of a named review template so a judge config id pins to an exact template version.

nodes.name: derive_judge_config_id
nodes.summary: Derives a JudgeConfigId from a review artifact's template name, model, and template content hash.

nodes.name: levels.py
nodes.summary: Defines the artifact level taxonomy that groups review types for comparability, and derives the level for a given review type.

nodes.name: ArtifactLevel
nodes.summary: Enumerates the artifact levels — the comparability grouping that agreement and dispersion reports are computed within.

nodes.name: derive_artifact_level
nodes.summary: Maps a review type onto its artifact level, raising rather than defaulting for unknown types.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Core Pydantic domain model for the metrology layer: project and judge identities, human sample verdicts, graduated configs, audit findings, runs, and the versioned record envelope.
nodes.languageNotes: MetrologyRecord is a versioned envelope with mutually exclusive payload fields, so one append-only store holds several record types safely.

nodes.name: ProjectId
nodes.summary: A project's stable identifier together with the source it was derived from.

nodes.name: JudgeResultRef
nodes.summary: Reference to a specific judge result artifact: its project, relative path, and content hash.

nodes.name: JudgeConfigId
nodes.summary: Identity of a judge configuration — template name, model, and template content hash.

nodes.name: SampleVerdict
nodes.summary: A recorded human ground-truth verdict on one judge result, with its note, artifact level, capture time, and blind flag.

nodes.name: GraduatedConfig
nodes.summary: A judge configuration that has graduated at a given artifact level, with the evidence snapshot that justified it.

nodes.name: AuditCategory
nodes.summary: Canonical enumeration of audit finding categories that raw agent output is normalised onto.

nodes.name: AuditSeverity
nodes.summary: The audit's own critical/high/medium/low severity scale, deliberately disjoint from review severity.

nodes.name: AuditFinding
nodes.summary: One normalised audit finding with its category, severity, effort, location, and summary, retaining the raw category it came from.

nodes.name: AuditRun
nodes.summary: A single recorded audit run: project, commit, prompt hash, model, timestamp, findings, and count of values that failed to normalise.

nodes.name: AuditNoiseFloor
nodes.summary: The measured run-to-run variance for a project and prompt hash, in total and per category.

nodes.name: MetrologyRecord
nodes.summary: Versioned envelope wrapping any single metrology payload — sample, graduated config, audit run, or noise floor — for the append-only store.

nodes.name: preemption.py
nodes.summary: Generates, writes, and freshness-checks pre-emption fragments — short static guidance rendered from a stored audit baseline that a pipeline can prepend to a dispatch prompt.

nodes.name: _sanitize_project_id
nodes.summary: Sanitises a project id into a filesystem-safe fragment filename component.

nodes.name: render_fragment
nodes.summary: Renders a pre-emption fragment from a baseline, emitting a header stamped with the source prompt hash and measurement time plus fixed per-category guidance.

nodes.name: write_fragment
nodes.summary: Writes a rendered pre-emption fragment to disk under the target directory, creating it if needed.

nodes.name: read_fragment_header
nodes.summary: Parses a stored fragment's stamped header to recover the baseline identity it was generated from.

nodes.name: read_fragment_body
nodes.summary: Reads the guidance body of a stored fragment, excluding its provenance header.

nodes.name: check_freshness
nodes.summary: Compares a stored fragment's stamped provenance against the current baseline and reports whether it is stale.

nodes.name: report.py
nodes.summary: Computes the metrology reports from captured samples — agreement between judge and human, dispersion across judge configs, and agreement trend over time — after enriching each sample from its review artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: Samples whose judge result has gone stale or whose template is unversioned are excluded and counted, never silently folded into the rates.

nodes.name: EnrichedSample
nodes.summary: A captured sample joined to its review artifact: judge verdict, artifact level, source document, and whether it is admissible.

nodes.name: _enrich_one
nodes.summary: Enriches one captured sample by re-reading its review artifact, re-deriving identity, and marking it inadmissible when stale or unversioned.

nodes.name: enrich_samples
nodes.summary: Enriches a list of captured samples, returning the enriched records for report computation.

nodes.name: agreement_report
nodes.summary: Computes the agreement report — judge-versus-human match rate per comparable group — with below-floor marking and an exclusion summary.

nodes.name: dispersion_report
nodes.summary: Computes the dispersion report, measuring how often different judge configs disagree on the same source artifact.

nodes.name: _bucket_label
nodes.summary: Formats a capture timestamp into the label for its trend bucket.

nodes.name: trend_report
nodes.summary: Computes agreement and dispersion per time bucket to produce the trend report series.

nodes.name: report_models.py
nodes.summary: Typed Pydantic output shapes for the metrology reports — group keys, agreement and dispersion cells, exclusion summaries, and trend series.

nodes.name: AgreementReport
nodes.summary: The agreement report: one cell per comparable group plus a summary of excluded samples.

nodes.name: DispersionReport
nodes.summary: The dispersion report: one cell per artifact plus a summary of excluded samples.

nodes.name: TrendReport
nodes.summary: Time-bucketed series of agreement and dispersion snapshots.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Append-only JSON record store for the metrology layer, with atomic writes, schema-version enforcement, and typed readers for samples, graduations, audit runs, and noise floors.
nodes.languageNotes: Records are written atomically to per-record files and re-read through a schema-version check that raises rather than silently reading an incompatible record.

nodes.name: resolve_store_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the metrology store directory from configuration, defaulting to the user-level metrology home.

nodes.name: _judge_config_matches
nodes.summary: Compares a stored judge config against a wanted one for lookup filtering.

nodes.name: MetrologyStore
nodes.summary: The metrology store itself: writes samples, graduations, audit runs, and noise floors atomically, and reads them back with schema-version validation.

nodes.name: judge.py
nodes.summary: Judge threshold contract for pipeline actions: resolves effective pass and concerns floors from template and step overrides, and derives the enforced verdict from a review score.
nodes.languageNotes: Provenance records whether a threshold came from the template or a step override, so an enforced verdict is always attributable.

nodes.name: JudgeThresholds
nodes.summary: The effective pass and concerns score floors, with a derive_verdict method mapping a score onto a verdict.

nodes.name: resolve_thresholds
nodes.summary: Resolves effective judge thresholds by layering a step override over the template's declared values, recording provenance.

nodes.name: enforce_judge
nodes.summary: Applies the resolved thresholds to a review result, deriving and logging the enforced verdict.

nodes.name: protocol.py
nodes.summary: Declares the runtime-checkable EventAction protocol that every user-definable event action must satisfy.
nodes.languageNotes: typing.Protocol with @runtime_checkable; name/events are plain attributes rather than properties to avoid ceremony.

nodes.name: EventAction
nodes.summary: Protocol specifying an action's namespaced name, the events it may bind to, an async execute, and a config validate.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic validation layer for events.yaml, converting raw YAML into typed schema models that manifest.py then lowers into runtime dataclasses.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors pipeline/schema.py's split between Pydantic validation models and the runtime dataclass shape.

nodes.name: BindingEntrySchema
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for one {action, params} binding entry, forbidding extra keys and rejecting an empty action name.

nodes.name: EventManifestSchema
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for the whole events.yaml document, validating that every bindings key names a known EventType.

nodes.name: parse_manifest_yaml
nodes.summary: Validates a raw parsed YAML mapping into an EventManifestSchema, attributing validation errors to the manifest path.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Root of the pipeline actions package: exports the Action protocol, the canonical ActionType enum, and the action-type registry used by the executor.

nodes.name: ActionType
nodes.summary: Canonical StrEnum of pipeline action type identifiers (dispatch, review, summary, compact, checkpoint, cf-op, commit, gate).

nodes.name: get_action
nodes.summary: Resolves a registered Action implementation by its action type, raising when the type is unknown.

nodes.name: checkpoint.py
